Description: On the QLAdmin dividend screen, the Accrued Interest figure is showing as a negative number — one policy reads -$126.93 against a balance of $9,220.33. QLAdmin works out accrued interest by counting forward from the Interest Paid To date, and we have been loading the wrong date into that field: the date premiums are paid to, rather than the date interest was last credited. On that policy the two are five months apart, so QLAdmin counts backwards and produces a negative figure.
Notes: Fixed in v58.37 and validated. The interest dates were in the accounting extract and the converter was already reading them, but it filed them under a different policy number format than it later looked them up under, so it never found a single one and quietly fell back to the premium date. The converter now files them under both formats. QuikDvdp was rebuilt: all 59 policies holding a dividend balance now carry their real interest paid-to date and a year-to-date interest figure, where before none did. The 16 that displayed a future date — the ones producing negative accrued interest — are down to zero. Dividend balances themselves are untouched and the row count is unchanged at 5,083. Interest rates were not changed; Eric confirmed the QLAdmin rates are correct. The rebuilt table is in Output/Test_Validation for review in a test region. Full-batch regression still to run before closure.
